answer.rationale: Finance mandates an 18% cut and the incumbent has refused to reopen price, so renewal cannot meet the cost objective; deferral leaves the line exposed when the contract lapses in 14 days. Memory c2 indicates the low-cost vendor previously cut unit cost sharply with quick onboarding and accurate invoicing, but it is a single archived data point from last year and conditions may have changed, so I want its source verified before committing. Memory c3 supports dual-sourcing as risk protection, which is relevant because the line runs at 94% of committed volume with no buffer — a full switch now would be reckless. Given capacity for exactly one decision, I intend a guarded, partial shift: move a limited volume tranche to the low-cost vendor to begin capturing savings and validate current performance, while keeping the incumbent on interim terms for the remainder to protect delivery. Confidence is moderate because the vendor's current capacity, quality, and pricing are unverified and the 14-day window is tight.
